target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Some deployments serve a Claude/MiniMax model through a proxy that intermittently degrades a native `tool_use` block into plain text. In that degraded case the tool call arrives as the namespaced/bare XML attribute dialect — `<invoke name="tool"><parameter name="x">v</parameter></invoke>`, optionally wrapped in `<function_calls>...</function_calls>` and optionally prefixed with `antml:` or `mm:`.

On current `main` two gaps remained:

1. The visible-text sanitizer recognized the `antml:` prefix but not the `mm:` prefix, so a degraded `mm:invoke` block leaked verbatim into the user-visible reply.
2. The persist-path stripper (`packages/tool-call-repair` `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks`) did not recognize the attribute-dialect invoke at all, so an unfenced standalone degraded invoke block was written into the durable `done.message` instead of being scrubbed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user, and it must not be persisted into session state either — but a legitimate code example of the same markup (inside a fenced or inline code span) must be preserved, not deleted. This change teaches both layers about the full attribute dialect using a closed `(?:antml:|mm:)?` namespace allow-list, so arbitrary `ns:` tokens in prose are never matched.

This PR was re-implemented on top of current `main` after upstream refactored the tool-call-repair package (the new `scanXmlishToolCall` seam and code-region helpers). The change is scoped to the net delta that still reproduces on `main`:

- **Visible text** (`assistant-visible-text.ts`): mirror the existing `antml:` handling for the `mm:` namespace in the tag-name scan, quick-check, and payload-start patterns. The `<function_calls>`-wrapped bare-invoke case is already scrubbed by the package strip stage in the delivery pipeline.
- **Persist path** (`packages/tool-call-repair`): a dedicated linear scanner recognizes a complete standalone invoke block (bare/`antml:`/`mm:`, `<function_calls>` wrapper, self-closing, and zero-parameter forms). The scanner returns `none`/`incomplete`/`complete`, so on an unterminated open the strip loop bails and preserves the remainder — exactly mirroring the existing dialects — keeping the scan linear on adversarial input.
- **Code-region awareness**: the strip takes an optional code-region predicate evaluated at the block's start offset. Fenced/inline Markdown examples of the invoke dialect are preserved while unfenced standalone leaked blocks are scrubbed. Without a predicate the package strip lazily computes code regions so a bare call still spares examples.
- **Plugin SDK contract preserved**: the exported `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` stays strict by default (it forces a scrub of every region, even inside code, for untrusted callers), with code-aware behavior available only via the explicit `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }` opt-in.
- **Layering**: `findCodeRegions`/`isInsideCode`/`CodeRegion` were moved into `normalization-core` (the package's only dependency) so `tool-call-repair` can share one implementation without importing app source; `src/shared/text/code-regions.ts` re-exports them so existing callers are unaffected.

Non-goals/boundaries: the native Anthropic/DSML transports are untouched; no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced; the equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged; the invoke dialect is recognized only by the strip/sanitize paths (never promoted to an executable call and never wired into the stream-buffering scanner).

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude/MiniMax routes no longer see raw namespaced/bare `invoke` tool-call XML in their replies, and the leaked block is no longer written into the persisted message (no session-state content loss). Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped. A resolved-review audit also removed an O(n²) worst case on the persist strip path, so adversarial degraded text cannot cause pathological CPU use.

## Evidence

Focused regression tests were added at the layers that own the contract:
- `packages/tool-call-repair/src/payload.test.ts`: invoke-dialect variants (bare/`antml:`/`mm:`, `function_calls` wrapper, self-closing, zero-param), code-region preservation vs. unfenced scrub, the predicate override, and a linear-time guard against many unterminated opens.
- `src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts`: the `preserveCodeRegions` opt-in and strict default.
- `src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.test.ts`: the `mm:invoke`/`mm:parameter` visible-text case (parallel to the existing `antml:` case), alongside existing standalone-vs-inline `function_calls` delivery-path coverage.

Real-behavior proof (before = current `main`, after = this branch), driving the actual `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` and `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` on the leak shapes:

```
=== BEFORE (main) ===
A2 mm-visible       => "Working on it.\n<mm:invoke name=\"get_weather\">\n<mm:parameter name=\"city\">Paris</mm:parameter>\n</mm:invoke>"
A3 bare-fc-visible  => "Done.\n<function_calls>\n<invoke name=\"get_weather\">\n<parameter name=\"city\">Paris</parameter>\n</invoke>\n</function_calls>"
C1 persist-unfenced => "Here you go.\n<invoke name=\"get_weather\">\n<parameter name=\"city\">Paris</parameter>\n</invoke>"
B1 persist-fenced   => "...```xml\n<invoke ...>...\n```..."   (preserved)
B2 persist-inline   => "Use the `<invoke name=\"get_weather\">` opener to start."   (preserved)

=== AFTER (this branch) ===
A2 mm-visible       => "Working on it."
A3 bare-fc-visible  => "Done."
C1 persist-unfenced => "Here you go.\n"
B1 persist-fenced   => "...```xml\n<invoke ...>...\n```..."   (still preserved)
B2 persist-inline   => "Use the `<invoke name=\"get_weather\">` opener to start."   (still preserved)
```

The three real leak shapes (A2 visible `mm:`, A3 visible `function_calls`-wrapped bare invoke, C1 persisted unfenced standalone invoke) are now scrubbed, while the fenced (B1) and inline (B2) code examples remain untouched — the exact over-scrub concern is verified closed.

O(n²) audit fix: a resolved-review pass measured the persist strip degrading quadratically on adversarial input with many unterminated invoke opens (720 KB ≈ 977 ms, scaling to seconds for a few MB). Making the scanner bail on `incomplete` (mirroring the existing unterminated-candidate bail) brought the same 720 KB input to ≈ 0.8 ms and restored linear scaling; a regression test locks this.

Verification: `tool-call-repair` grammar/payload/stream-normalizer (157 passed), `provider-stream-shared` + `tool-payload` + `assistant-visible-text` + `sanitize-text` + `message-action-runner.send-validation` + `embedded-agent-utils` (all green), `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` exit 0, `plugin-sdk:api:check` and `plugin-sdk:surface:check` exit 0 (surface budget bumped by the one new `StripPlainTextToolCallOptions` type), oxfmt clean, `git diff --check` clean. Rebased onto current `main` (`9b823c61`).

Fixes an issue where Google Meet chrome-node realtime sessions could retain an expired audio wait every 250 ms while a call was silent. Long quiet periods therefore grew node-local polling state until audio eventually arrived or the bridge stopped.

target.body:
## Context capsule

This is PR1/5 in the clean release-head durable core replacement stack. It is docs/RFC only: it establishes the durable-core boundary, root-cause model, value proposition, and validation plan before implementation PRs claim runtime behavior.

The replacement stack is rebased onto latest `release/2026.7.1` so maintainers and ClawSweeper can review a clean topology without the old beta3 cumulative CI drift.

## Durable core stack overview

Durable core is the shared, opt-in runtime substrate that records accepted work identity, ordered steps/events, parent-child links, bounded refs, recovery states, wake/attention obligations, delivery evidence, and read-only inspection for long-running OpenClaw agent/session/task/subagent work.

It is needed because OpenClaw can accept long-running work, delegate it, defer it, route it through channels, or recover after restart without one consistent durable obligation that later code can inspect, recover, acknowledge, or fail closed. The recurring failure class includes coordinator silence, restart/interruption loss, stale running work, parent/child handoff gaps, delivery/attention uncertainty, and side-effect uncertainty.

The core sits below Task Flow, Workboard, plugins, sessions, and channel UI. Those surfaces may project from durable facts, but they should not own the persistence boundary.

Stack order:
1. PR1/5 — docs/RFC/root-cause/boundary anchor and proof plan.
2. PR2/5 — runtime foundation/core and persisted durable state invariants.
3. PR3/5 — wake targets, durable producers, replay/recovery semantics.
4. PR4/5 — controls/inspection plus CLI/Gateway integration surface.
5. PR5/5 — internal session delivery handoff for resolved session targets.

Current PR: **PR1/5 — durable runtime RFC/docs**.

## Stack position

- Stack item: PR1/5
- Current PR summary: adds the durable core architecture RFC, test/proof plan, docs map entries, and i18n glossary labels.
- Dependency/base: `openclaw/openclaw:release/2026.7.1` at `09229c7aaad60c6ed1ec3bde685f191299148776`
- This PR head: `mjnkao/openclaw:codex/openclaw-durable-release-head-pr1-rfc-20260714` at `3cb8fea1bc63ef52a5d815dfb5ec620aaade1bc6`
- Focused diff range: `09229c7aaad60c6ed1ec3bde685f191299148776..3cb8fea1bc63ef52a5d815dfb5ec620aaade1bc6`
- Downstream dependency: PR2/5 runtime core depends on this RFC/docs base.
- Supersedes: replaces earlier reviewed PR #104246 after the release branch advanced.
- Does not claim: runtime behavior, wake replay, CLI/Gateway controls, session handoff, external transport delivery, or product retry/resume policy.

## Dependency / promotion gate

- This PR should be reviewed as the PR1/5 docs/RFC slice on top of `release/2026.7.1`.
- The next PR should not be promoted until this PR reaches the agreed review threshold (`>= platinum hermit`) or maintainers explicitly waive the gate.
- If ClawSweeper asks for proof/fixes here, the stack pauses on this PR until those are addressed.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can accept long-running work, delegate it to subagents, defer it through waits, route it through channels, and recover after restarts. Today those flows do not share one durable obligation model that later code can inspect, recover, acknowledge, or fail closed.

The repeated failure class is broader than one channel, UI, plugin, or task surface:

- coordinator silence after delegated or detached work;
- restart/interruption loss where accepted work has no inspectable recovery obligation;
- stale running sessions/tasks that are hard to distinguish from actively owned work;
- parent/child handoff gaps between sessions, subagents, and task runners;
- wake/attention uncertainty after a result or recovery signal exists;
- delivery uncertainty where internal ownership, external transport, and user-visible consumption can be conflated;
- side-effect uncertainty when retries or repairs are attempted without a durable evidence trail.

This PR defines the generic durable-core boundary and root-cause model so later implementation PRs can be reviewed against the actual failure class instead of one-off symptoms.

## User value

For OpenClaw users and operators, durable core aims to make long-running work safer and easier to trust:

- accepted work can be inspected after silence or restart;
- recovery state can be explained instead of guessed;
- duplicate retries and ghost work are easier to prevent;
- parent/child handoffs become auditable;
- operators get safer read-only inspection before repair;
- product surfaces can build higher-level workflows without each inventing its own persistence boundary.

## Why this is upstream-friendly

This PR intentionally starts with docs/RFC and proof boundaries before runtime changes. It is upstream-friendly because it:

- defines the shared core boundary before adding implementation weight;
- keeps durable core opt-in and below product-specific surfaces;
- avoids making Task Flow, Workboard, plugins, sessions, or channel UI own the persistence contract;
- separates internal durable evidence from external/user-visible delivery claims;
- gives maintainers a sequential stack with focused review slices;
- keeps migration, schema, and runtime risk deferred to implementation PRs with explicit proof gates;
- makes rollback/review boundaries clearer than a single monolithic PR.

## Scope

- Durable core architecture RFC.
- Root-cause analysis and failure taxonomy.
- Test/proof plan for later implementation PRs.
- Docs map and docs navigation updates.
- zh-CN glossary entries for new/changed doc labels.
- Stack framing and review boundaries.

## Non-scope

- No runtime behavior.
- No database/schema migration.
- No CLI/Gateway controls.
- No worker loop or wake replay implementation.
- No plugin/channel delivery behavior.
- No Task Flow or Workboard product feature implementation.

target.title: fix(exec-approvals): handle same-process sync/async lock contention
target.body:
## Problem

The exec-approvals store uses two lock mechanisms sharing the same `.lock` file:

1. **Async sidecar lock** (via `@openclaw/fs-safe`): Used by `resolveExecApprovalsLocked`, `updateExecApprovals`, `loadExecApprovalsAsync`. Has `allowReentrant: true`.

2. **Sync custom lock** (`acquireExecApprovalsLockSync`): Used by `loadExecApprovals`, `readExecApprovalsSnapshot`, `resolveExecApprovals`.

When the async lock holds the `.lock` file (e.g., during `ensureExecApprovalsSnapshot`), the sync lock attempts fail immediately because `acquireExecApprovalsLockSync` detects `ownerPid === process.pid` and treats it as self-deadlock — it does not retry. The failure triggers `createFailClosedExecApprovalsFallback()` → `security: "deny"`. All subsequent execs see `security=deny` and are denied.

The key condition in `acquireExecApprovalsLockSync`:
```typescript
if (state.ownerPid !== null && state.ownerPid !== process.pid && attempt < RETRIES) {
    sleepExecApprovalsSyncLockRetry();
    continue;
}
throw error; // Falls through for same-PID → immediate fail
```

## Fix

Added `isExecApprovalsProcessLocalLockContention()` to detect this specific scenario: `file_lock_timeout` error where the lock is owned by the current process and the target file already exists.

Modified `withExecApprovalsReadLockSync()` to catch same-process contention in both code paths and fall back to lockless reads.

### Why this is safe

- Async writes use atomic temp-file + rename → concurrent reads always see a consistent snapshot
- Only applies to **read** locks — write serialization is preserved
- Lockless fallback only triggers when the **target file already exists**, preserving fail-closed behavior during initial policy creation (no file yet → writer must not be bypassed)

## Changes

- `src/infra/exec-approvals.ts`: Added `isExecApprovalsProcessLocalLockContention()` helper + modified `withExecApprovalsReadLockSync()` (both code paths)
- `src/infra/exec-approvals-store.test.ts`: Added test that simulates same-process lock contention and verifies `loadExecApprovals()` and `readExecApprovalsSnapshot()` return real policy instead of fail-closed deny

## Testing

All 72 exec-approvals store tests pass, including the new test and the existing "fails closed when a writer locks the store before creating the policy file" test (which verifies the fail-closed path is preserved when the target file doesn't exist).

Closes #106777

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Same-process sync/async lock contention in exec-approvals causes all exec commands to be denied with security=deny when the async sidecar lock is held during synchronous policy reads (issue #106777).

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node.js v24.16.0, OpenClaw gateway running locally with single-process mode.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```
cd /mnt/data/repos/forks/openclaw
npx vitest run src/infra/exec-approvals-store.test.ts --no-coverage
```

**Evidence after fix**:
```
RUN  v4.1.9 /mnt/data/repos/forks/openclaw

 ✓  infra  ../../src/infra/exec-approvals-store.test.ts (72 tests) 435ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  72 passed (72)
   Start at  20:21:35
   Duration  911ms (transform 332ms, setup 231ms, import 122ms, tests 435ms, environment 0ms)
```

**Observed result after fix**: All 72 tests pass including the new same-process lock contention test (verifies loadExecApprovals and readExecApprovalsSnapshot return real policy instead of fail-closed deny) and the existing fail-closed test (verifies deny when target file does not exist). The lockless read fallback correctly activates only for same-PID contention when the policy file already exists.

**What was not tested**: Multi-process lock contention across separate gateway instances (requires Docker or multi-node setup). Windows-specific file locking behavior. Production gateway with high-frequency concurrent exec calls.

target.title: fix(signal): reject hex/exponent text-style span offsets
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Signal container sends could apply the wrong styled span when `text-style` start/length tokens used JavaScript-only forms such as `0x10` or `1e1`. Those tokens were coerced with `Number(...)` into different offsets, so bold/italic markers could land on the wrong characters or invent spans that the caller never intended.

## Why This Change Was Made

Parse `text-style` `start`/`length` with the same `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` helper already used for container quote timestamps. target.title: fix(scripts): bound conflict-marker scan reads to prevent OOM on large files
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`pnpm check:no-conflict-markers` previously read every candidate tracked file returned by `git grep` into memory whole via `fs.readFileSync`. A single large generated or text file that slipped through the binary heuristic could exhaust the process memory before the scan completed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Replace the tracked-files scan with `git grep -n -z -o -I -E` so only exact conflict-marker matches are returned.
- Parse the grep output (path, line number, match) into violation records without buffering file contents.
- Keep `findConflictMarkersInFiles` for direct, small-scale use; the tracked-files path no longer reads files whole.
- `findConflictMarkersInTrackedFiles` now returns paths relative to the repository root, matching `git grep` output.

## User Impact

- Normal conflict-marker checks on source and documentation files are unchanged.
- Oversized or generated files can no longer cause an OOM during the scan because their contents are never read.
- CI and pre-commit runs remain robust against accidental large-file commits.

## Evidence

Local focused test passes:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts --run
```

Result:

```
✓ |tooling| test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts (9 tests) 585ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  9 passed (9)
```

Added regression tests covering:
- tracked files with conflict markers reported via `git grep`
- clean tracked files returning no violations
- binary tracked files skipped by `git grep -I`

- large files whose line numbers are reported without reading the whole file

## What Problem This Solves

Closes #107391.

The macOS Skills settings model cached the first `skills.status` response. If the view loaded before the local node reconnected, the UI could keep showing a skill as unavailable even after the Gateway reported it as eligible.

target.title: fix(utils): log JSON parse error when both JSON and JSON5 parsers fail
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When both `JSON.parse` and `JSON5.parse` fail for the same input, the `JSON.parse` error (which may contain useful diagnostic information 鈥?e.g., the specific character position where strict JSON parsing failed) is silently discarded. Callers only see the `JSON5.parse` error, losing context about why the input failed the strict JSON path first. This makes debugging malformed config/manifest files unnecessarily difficult.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wrapped the `json5.parse(raw)` call in a nested try-catch. When both parsers fail, the original `JSON.parse` error is logged via `console.warn` before the `JSON5.parse` error is re-thrown. This preserves backward compatibility (the throw behavior is unchanged) while adding diagnostic context.

## User Impact

- Fast path unchanged: valid JSON still parses directly via `JSON.parse`
- Fallback unchanged: valid JSON5 (trailing commas, comments, etc.) still parses via `json5.parse`
- Only change: when **both** parsers fail, a warning with the JSON error message is emitted before the throw, giving operators/debuggers visibility into the failure

## Evidence / Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Silent error swallowing 鈥?`JSON.parse` error discarded when falling through to `json5.parse`. The fix preserves and logs the JSON error.
- **Real environment tested:** Node.js runtime with vitest; `console.warn` behavior verified via `vi.spyOn`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  npx vitest run src/utils/parse-json-compat.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```
   鉁?parseJsonWithJson5Fallback > parses strict JSON object
   鉁?parseJsonWithJson5Fallback > parses strict JSON array
   鉁?parseJsonWithJson5Fallback > parses JSON null and boolean literals
   鉁?parseJsonWithJson5Fallback > parses JSON number and string primitives
   鉁?parseJsonWithJson5Fallback > parses JSON5 with trailing comma
   鉁?parseJsonWithJson5Fallback > parses JSON5 with single-line comment
   鉁?parseJsonWithJson5Fallback > parses JSON5 with block comment
   鉁?parseJsonWithJson5Fallback > parses JSON5 with single-quoted keys
   鉁?parseJsonWithJson5Fallback > parses JSON5 with unquoted keys
   鉁?parseJsonWithJson5Fallback > throws when both parsers fail and warns about the JSON parse error
   鉁?parseJsonWithJson5Fallback > includes the JSON parse error message in the warning
   鉁?parseJsonWithJson5Fallback > warns only once per call for dual-failure input
   鉁?parseJsonWithJson5Fallback > accepts custom json5 parser
   鉁?parseJsonWithJson5Fallback > re-throws custom parser error after logging JSON parse failure

   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  14 passed (14)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** When both parsers fail (e.g., `"not valid"`), `console.warn` is called once with the `JSON.parse` error message before the `JSON5.parse` error is re-thrown. 14 tests pass: 4 strict JSON fast-path, 5 JSON5 fallback, 3 dual-failure diagnostic, 2 custom parser.
- **What was not tested:** Integration with actual config loading (`src/config/io.ts`). The fix only adds diagnostic logging on a path that already threw; the throw behavior is unchanged.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Coverage level:** Unit test
- **Target test file:** `src/utils/parse-json-compat.test.ts` (new)
- **Scenario locked in:** Strict JSON parsing (object, array, primitives), JSON5 fallback (trailing comma, line comment, block comment, single-quoted keys, unquoted keys), dual-failure warning message content and call count, custom parser delegation and error re-throw.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** `parseJsonWithJson5Fallback` is a pure utility with no side effects. 14 focused tests cover all code paths: the fast path, the fallback path, and the new error-logging path in the catch clause.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** The `catch` block in `parseJsonWithJson5Fallback` silently discarded the `JSON.parse` error when falling through to `json5.parse`. When `json5.parse` also failed, the `JSON.parse` error was lost and only the `JSON5.parse` error was thrown.
- **Missing detection / guardrail:** No logging or wrapping of the original `JSON.parse` error when both parsers fail.

target.title: fix(discord): add timeout to guarded gateway metadata fetches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Discord gateway metadata HTTP through `fetchDiscordGatewayMetadataGuarded` could hang in DNS/proxy preflight because the `/gateway/bot` deadline lived only in `init.signal`, while `fetchWithSsrFGuard` aborts preflight from its top-level `signal`. A stalled Discord API / proxy preflight could block gateway startup until process restart.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper P1: forward the existing `withAbortTimeout` AbortSignal as the guard's top-level `signal`, and keep a single deadline owner:

- When `init.signal` is present (production `/gateway/bot` path): pass `{ signal: callerSignal }` only — no second `timeoutMs` timer
- When unsignaled: install `timeoutMs` hang floor (default 30s / `gatewayInfoTimeoutMs`)
- Thread resolved `gatewayInfoTimeoutMs` through `createDiscordGatewayMetadataFetch` / invalid-proxy fallback for the unsignaled hang floor

No new config/env surface.

## User Impact

**Before:** A stalled Discord metadata DNS/proxy preflight ignored the gateway metadata abort signal and could hang forever.

**After:** The same `/gateway/bot` timeout AbortSignal cancels guarded-fetch preflight and fetch. Unsignaled guarded metadata calls still fail closed after the configured hang floor.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-metadata.ts`, `gateway-plugin.ts`
- Regressions: `gateway-metadata.test.ts`, `gateway-plugin.test.ts`
- Production caller: `createDiscordGatewayPlugin` → `fetchDiscordGatewayInfoWithTimeout` → `fetchDiscordGatewayMetadataGuarded` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard`

### Unit + wrapper-level hung-peer / stalled-preflight

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-metadata.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-plugin.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

```text

 ✓ |extension-discord| ... > aborts stalled DNS preflight when the gateway metadata init signal fires 76ms
 ✓ |extension-discord| ... > aborts when the shared guarded fetch times out before headers arrive 261ms
 ✓ |extension-discord| ... > times out hung loopback responses through the production timeout owner path 254ms
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  26 passed (26)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 3.69s
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Guarded Discord gateway metadata fetches observe the `/gateway/bot` abort signal during DNS/proxy preflight; unsignaled calls keep a hang floor.
- **Canonical reachability path:** `createDiscordGatewayPlugin` → `fetchDiscordGatewayInfoWithTimeout` (`withAbortTimeout` → `init.signal`) → `fetchDiscordGatewayMetadataGuarded` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard({ signal })`.
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime HTTP; loopback `node:http` peer that accepts TCP without writing headers; stalled DNS preflight via injected `lookupFn` on the real guard while the Discord wrapper owns signal wiring.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused `DEFAULT_DISCORD_GATEWAY_INFO_TIMEOUT_MS` / `resolveDiscordGatewayInfoTimeoutMs` and `fetchWithSsrFGuard` top-level `signal` contract; no new Discord config key.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` + `node --import tsx` standalone hung-peer harness.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-metadata.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-plugin.test.ts --reporter=verbose
PROOF_MODE=short node --import tsx /tmp/discord-gateway-metadata-timeout-proof.mjs
```

- **Evidence after fix (Vitest):**

```text

 ✓ |extension-discord| ... > aborts stalled DNS preflight when the gateway metadata init signal fires 76ms
 ✓ |extension-discord| ... > aborts when the shared guarded fetch times out before headers arrive 261ms
 ✓ |extension-discord| ... > times out hung loopback responses through the production timeout owner path 254ms
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  26 passed (26)
```

- **Evidence after fix (standalone hung peer):**

```text
[standalone] source_signal_forward=true source_no_duplicate_timer=true source_withAbortTimeout_owner=true production_timeout_ms=30000
[standalone] mode=short hang_http_peer=http://127.0.0.1:57918/gateway/bot caller=fetchDiscordGatewayInfoWithTimeout→fetchDiscordGatewayMetadataGuarded→fetchWithSsrFGuard timeoutMs=250
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Wrapper forwards `init.signal` as top-level guard `signal` (no duplicate `timeoutMs` when signaled); stalled DNS preflight aborts without dispatching fetch; hung loopback headers abort near the configured deadline.
- **What was not tested:** Live Discord API `/gateway/bot` against production Discord; full Gateway reconnect storm; full 30s production-floor duration (proof uses a 250ms stand-in).
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

## Risk / Compatibility

Low. Default remains the existing 30s gateway-info timeout. Operator `gatewayInfoTimeoutMs` / env override continue through the same resolver. Signaled production path uses one cancellation owner; unsignaled path keeps the hang floor.

target.body:
## Upstream cumulative PR / focused review target

This PR is opened directly against `openclaw/openclaw:release/2026.7.1` because GitHub cannot target an upstream PR at another fork PR branch. It is therefore cumulative in the GitHub "Files changed" view.

**Focused review target:** please review the immediate predecessor diff `ea4627cfeaf507bee5d6c3b3f18419e669fcb60a..be7e16817cd71fef0bbecdc6c847aecdad971c6b` (PR4′ (this stack immediate predecessor) → PR5′ head). The cumulative ancestry is intentional and verified.


@clawsweeper review

Historical reviewed predecessor: old upstream #106443 covered the earlier version of this slice. It is useful review context only; please review this current upstream PR/head/base package fresh.

# PR5/5 - internal session delivery handoff + final hardening

## What Problem This Solves

This finishes the clean upstream durable-core stack by turning resolved durable wake
obligations into an internal session delivery-queue handoff on gateway startup.
After PR4 made wakes inspectable and controllable, PR5 gives the durable runtime
a concrete recovery path: a resolved wake is replayed, persisted with delivery
evidence, and queued for the owning OpenClaw session without inventing external
channel sends.

## Stack position

- Stack item: PR5/5
- PR: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106443
- Clean PR5 comparison: `a30e2b6ce4e5f1390599380aedc82078c98854f7..443ffd2292e146fad3c089a03382a5f4702632f7`
- PR4 dependency: `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/105844`
- GitHub base rationale: existing PR1-PR4 stack PRs target `release/2026.7.1`; the PR4 branch exists on the fork, not as an upstream base branch, so this PR follows stack convention while documenting the exact PR4-head diff.

## Scope

- Adds `createDurableWakeSessionDeliveryHook`, which resolves durable wakes to
  agent/session keys and enqueues one internal `systemEvent` via the session
  delivery queue.
- Wires gateway startup durable wake replay through that hook.
- Persists delivery evidence with `internalDelivery: "session_delivery_queue"`
  and `noExternalSend: true`.
- Extends focused replay/startup tests for idempotency, startup replay, ambiguous
  target handling, and no autonomous resume/abandon/create-new policy.
- Updates durable docs to clarify the `delivered` state and CLI wake-attempt
  evidence.

## Non-scope

- No Discord, Signal, Slack, plugin, or other external transport delivery is
  implemented or claimed.
- No cron mutation.
- No release/changelog/package churn from the stale old PR5 ancestry.
- No broad durable orchestration policy changes beyond this internal handoff.

## Evidence

Clean scope:

```text
6 files changed, 372 insertions(+), 50 deletions(-)
```

Focused behavior:

target.title: refactor(infra): add p-map concurrency limit to ports-inspect enrichment
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `enrichUnixListenerProcessInfo` and `readWindowsNetstatEntries` use `Promise.all` over all listeners/entries, spawning unbounded concurrent child-process operations. With many listeners on a single port (e.g., container port-forwarding, VPN tunnels), this triggers OOM/scheduler thrashing from dozens of simultaneous `ps` subprocesses.

**Solution**: Replace `Promise.all` with `pMap({concurrency: 20})`. Limits in-flight subprocesses to 20 per invocation. Each item's 3 `Promise.all` sub-tasks run within the same pMap slot, so peak subprocesses = 60, well within Linux default limits.

**What changed**: Two functions — `enrichUnixListenerProcessInfo` (line 201) and `readWindowsNetstatEntries` (line 523). Both use pMap with `concurrency: 20`. No signatures or behavior changed for callers.

**What did NOT change**: Unix listener parsing from `ss`/`lsof`, connection classification, Windows netstat/tasklist/wmic fallback, port matching, error handling. Zero logic changes beyond the concurrency wrapper.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: `enrichUnixListenerProcessInfo` iterates listeners and runs 3 `ps` sub-processes per item (`command=`, `user=`, `ppid=`). Without concurrency, N listeners = N×3 concurrent child processes. pMap `{concurrency: 20}` caps in-flight items to 20.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-35-generic, Node.js v25.9.0, p-map v7.0.3.

**Real-path evidence**: `inspectPortUsage()` called against real system listeners, exercising the patched `enrichUnixListenerProcessInfo` via its actual callers (`readUnixListeners`/`readUnixEstablishedConnections`). Each listener resolved through pMap({concurrency: 20}) spawning real `ps -p <pid> -o command=`, `ps -p <pid> -o user=`, `ps -p <pid> -o ppid=` subprocesses — exactly the patched code path used by `openclaw gateway run`, `openclaw daemon status`, and `openclaw dashboard`.

```

  inspectPortUsage → readUnixListeners → enrichUnixListenerProcessInfo
  Each listener: ps -p <pid> -o command= + user= + ppid= via pMap({concurrency:20})

[6768] PID=3303566 user=lizeyu ppid=2118    cmd="/opt/Orca/orca-ide"

```

✓ Real code path exercised: `inspectPortUsage()` → `readUnixListeners()` → `enrichUnixListenerProcessInfo()` via pMap
✓ Real `ps` subprocesses per listener — `command=`, `user=`, `ppid=`
✓ `pMap({concurrency: 20})` bounds in-flight child processes in the actual OpenClaw code

**pMap concurrency verification** (pMap behavior with 50 real PIDs, same pattern as patched code):

`pMap(50 items, async fn, {concurrency:20}) → max concurrent observed: 20/20 (limit honored), 50/50 completed, each item runs real `ps -p <pid>` child process.` Full output in concurrency proof section below. Same `concurrency: 20` value used in 7+ other codebase modules (cron service, gateway startup, media-understanding, agent sessions, tool catalog).

**What was not tested**: Physical Windows netstat path (no Windows CI runner). Windows path uses identical `pMap(entries, async fn, {concurrency: 20})` pattern — concurrency guarantee is identical by pMap library contract. The inner `Promise.all` (3 sub-tasks per item) remains unchanged because it batches per-item I/O, not across items.

**Lint fixed**: Restored blank lines between function declarations that were removed to offset added lines. Lint gate now passes.

## Concurrency=20 justification

- Linux `RLIMIT_NPROC` (non-root) defaults to ~30672 processes; 60 concurrent `ps` (20 items × 3 sub-calls) is negligible.
- Concurrency=20 matches 7+ existing pMap call sites in this codebase — it is the standard value for I/O-bound batch operations.
- Real measurement: each `ps -p <pid>` completes in 37–138ms on Linux 6.17; at concurrency=20, 50 items drain in ~2 seconds.

target.title: fix(wechat): preserve existing accounts across hot reload
target.body:
## Summary
- preserve known live accounts when an already-active channel hot-reload restarts without an explicit account id
- preserve known accounts for channel account-index reload markers such as `channels.openclaw-weixin.channelConfigUpdatedAt`
- avoid unioning stale manager-known accounts when a plugin channel was inactive before the same reload and becomes active afterward
- keep ordinary channel config reloads from resurrecting removed or disabled configured accounts
- treat hot-reload stop/restart as a manager-owned handoff only for channels that stayed active across plugin replacement
- document the WeChat multi-account behavior and cover the hot-reload paths with regression tests
- add a guard that ordinary caller-owned restarts still do not resurrect stale accounts
- harden the non-isolated agent model-catalog visibility coverage that timed out in refreshed CI

## Why
Adding a second WeChat account can temporarily surface only the new account in the plugin account listing. Before this change, the gateway could evict or fail to restart the already-running account during hot reload, leaving account A offline after account B logs in.

The latest repair covers the non-plugin account-index reload path called out by review: when a channel updates `channelConfigUpdatedAt`, the restart now includes manager-known accounts. The stale-account guard remains narrow because ordinary channel config edits still restart with the configured channel set only.

target.title: fix(secrets): collect persona-level TTS provider SecretRefs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Persona-level TTS provider API keys were not collected as SecretRefs and agent persona registry paths bound the wrong path segment as providerId (literal `providers` instead of `elevenlabs`). That breaks secrets plan/audit and runtime resolution for agent persona TTS keys.

Fixes #89607

## Summary

The secret collector walks `messages.tts.providers.*.apiKey` but does not walk `messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` or `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`. When a persona overrides the TTS provider config with a file-source SecretRef, the secret resolver never sees the ref, so the `apiKey` reaches the plugin as an unresolved object instead of the actual key string. The plugin then reports `not configured`.

This fix:
- Adds persona-level provider iteration in `collectTtsApiKeyAssignments`
- Registers two new target paths in the secret target registry (`messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` and `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`)
- Extends `hasAgentRuntimeSecretRefs` to detect persona-level TTS refs
- Adds 5 regression tests covering top-level, persona-level, combined, empty-persona, and agent-level persona paths

Closes #89607

## Evidence

Terminal output from `tsx` against the patched branch showing correct `providerId` binding and persona file SecretRef collection (see Real behavior proof for full capture).

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Agent persona TTS SecretRef paths must resolve `providerId` to the provider key (e.g. `elevenlabs`), not the literal `providers` segment, so plan/audit/runtime metadata match the configured provider. Persona-level file SecretRefs must be collected under `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS arm64, Node v22, OpenClaw branch `fix/tts-persona-secretref` at `/tmp/oc-89636`, commit after providerId index fix.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

  ```bash
  pnpm exec vitest run src/secrets/target-registry.test.ts src/secrets/runtime-config-collectors-tts.test.ts

  pnpm exec tsx /tmp/proof-tts-collect.mjs
  ```

- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from the patched source:

target.title: fix(line): honor channelData.line.mediaKind on the reply-token path
target.body: Closes #106512 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where a LINE bot that replies to an inbound message with a video or audio attachment — and sets `channelData.line.mediaKind` — has the media delivered as a **broken image** instead of a playable video/audio message. This affects the **reply-token path**, which is the path most inbound auto-replies take. `docs/channels/line.md` states the media kind is taken from `channelData.line.mediaKind` when set, and the proactive **push** path honors it — but the reply-token path ignored it and force-sent every media URL as an image. A user asking the bot for a video would receive a bubble that fails to render. ## Why This Change Was Made The reply-token delivery in `auto-reply-delivery.ts` built every media message with `createImageMessage(url)`, ignoring `mediaKind` / `previewImageUrl` / `durationMs` / `trackingId`, while the push adapter (`outbound.ts`) already resolved media through `resolveLineOutboundMedia` + `buildLineMediaMessageObject`. This change routes reply-token media through **those same helpers**, relocated to `outbound-media.ts` (their natural home next to `resolveLineOutboundMedia`) and reused by both paths — no parallel implementation. The network-touching resolver is injected into the delivery function as a `deps.buildMediaMessage` field and wired in `monitor.ts`, preserving the file's dependency-injection testability boundary (delivery-logic files do not import send primitives directly). Boundaries / non-goals: - **Generic media with no LINE-specific options keeps the image route**, matching the push path and the documented "generic media sends use the image route" behavior — no regression for the common bare-URL case. - A media that **cannot be built** (e.g. a video missing its `previewImageUrl`) surfaces as a **visible partial delivery** (the text still reaches the user), consistent with this file's existing partial-delivery handling. - The two delivery dispatchers (reply-token batch APIs vs proactive per-type primitives) remain **intentionally separate** and are **not** unified; only the leaf media-message builder is shared. ## User Impact LINE bots that reply with `channelData.line.mediaKind: "video"` or `"audio"` now deliver a correct, playable video/audio message on the reply-token path instead of a broken image bubble. No change for text-only replies or for generic media sends without LINE-specific options. ## Evidence **Real inbound → reply-token path (redacted live transcript).** A real LINE message was sent to the test-channel bot; its **fresh reply token** drove the **actual** `deliverLineAutoReply` on this branch (real `send.ts` `replyMessageLine`, no mocks). A media-only reply is used so the video rides the reply token (a text chunk would consume it), exercising the exact changed reply-token wiring end-to-end. LINE accepted the reply: ```text [2026-07-13T17:56:43.917Z] harness listening on :3000 (ngrok -> /line) [2026-07-13T17:56:51.093Z] inbound message from U4aef1…2a replyToken=9f1eb3…22 [2026-07-13T17:56:51.094Z] agent reply payload: media-only, channelData.line.mediaKind="video" [2026-07-13T17:56:51.190Z] -> replyMessageLine (REPLY TOKEN 9f1eb3…22) types=["video"] [2026-07-13T17:56:51.505Z] deliverLineAutoReply result = {"status":"delivered","replyTokenUsed":true} ``` The `replyMessageLine (REPLY TOKEN …) types=["video"]` line is the point: driven by a real inbound message, the fixed reply-token path delivered a **video** via the reply token (`replyTokenUsed: true`) — not a downgraded image and not a push fallback. On current-main this same flow would have sent `type:"image"`. **Live LINE app — before/after (real test channel).** The exact message objects the reply path builds were delivered to a LINE chat (push and reply render identically in the client). Same source clip `https://download.samplelib.com/mp4/sample-5s.mp4` in both cases; LINE returned `HTTP 200` for both. **修復前 (Before):** the reply path forced `{"type":"image","originalContentUrl":".../sample-5s.mp4"}`. LINE cannot render an mp4 as an image, so the bubble is a **broken placeholder**: **修復後 (After):** the reply path honors `mediaKind="video"` and builds `{"type":"video","originalContentUrl":".../sample-5s.mp4","previewImageUrl":".../clouds.jpg"}` → a **playable video bubble**: **Deterministic repro against the real functions** (real `resolveLineOutboundMedia` + `buildLineMediaMessageObject`, the exact `monitor.ts` wiring), same input clip, three outcomes: ``` OLD reply path (hardcoded): always -> {"type":"image","originalContentUrl":".../clip.mp4","previewImageUrl":".../clip.mp4"} NEW — channelData.line = { mediaKind:"video", previewImageUrl } -> status: delivered reply message sent: {"type":"video","originalContentUrl":".../clip.mp4","previewImageUrl":".../preview.jpg"} NEW — generic media, no LINE options (parity) -> status: delivered reply message sent: {"type":"image","originalContentUrl":".../clip.mp4","previewImageUrl":".../clip.mp4"} ``` **Unit tests** — `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-line.config.ts` on the touched suites (adds 3 reply-path media cases + a full `buildLineMediaMessageObject` / `hasLineSpecificMediaOptions` / `isLineUserTarget` suite): ``` Test Files 3 passed (3) Tests 44 passed (44) ``` **Red/green** — reverting only the reply-path media routing makes exactly the two new fix cases fail while the generic-image parity case stays green: ``` Tests 2 failed | 10 passed (12) × honors channelData.line.mediaKind ... expected "partial"/"video", received "delivered"/"image" ✓ keeps the image route for generic media without LINE-specific options ``` **Static checks** — `tsgo` extensions typecheck: pass · `pnpm lint:extensions` (oxlint): pass · `oxfmt --check` on touched files: pass. Branch **rebased onto current `main`** and re-verified. ---

target.title: fix(qqbot): allow approval buttons in direct C2C conversations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #107555. In QQ Bot direct (C2C) conversations, when `skill_workshop(action=apply)` or other plugin operations trigger an approval request, clicking the "Allow" button is always recorded as "Approval button rejected" in the Gateway log. The `plugin.approval.waitDecision` times out after ~70 seconds and returns "expired without a decision".

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #87154 added a command-authorization gate in `isImplicitApprovalButtonActorAuthorized()` that requires explicit non-wildcard `allowFrom` entries for all approval button clicks when no `execApprovals` is configured. This correctly prevents unauthorized group members from approving in group conversations.

However, this gate also blocks legitimate users in **direct (C2C) conversations** where:
- The conversation is inherently private (only the bot owner can interact)
- The approval request was delivered to the user's private chat
- `dmPolicy` may be `"open"` with a wildcard `allowFrom: ["*"]` (valid for DMs)

The command authorization check in `resolveQQBotSlashCommandAuthorized` / `resolveSlashCommandAuth` filters out wildcard entries and returns `false` when no explicit entries exist, causing all approval button clicks in direct conversations without explicit `allowFrom` to be rejected.

## Changes

- **`extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/interaction-handler.ts`**: In `isImplicitApprovalButtonActorAuthorized`, return `true` for direct (non-group) conversations without running the command authorization check. Group conversations still require explicit command authorization.
- **`extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/interaction-handler.test.ts`**: Added `it.each` test cases verifying that fallback approval buttons in direct C2C conversations resolve correctly even without an explicit allowlist or with a wildcard allowlist.

## User Impact

- Users with open DM policies (no `execApprovals` configured, wildcard or no `allowFrom`) can now click "Allow"/"Deny" on approval buttons in their direct conversations with the QQ Bot
- Group conversation approval button authorization is unchanged — explicit `allowFrom` entries are still required

## Evidence

- Root cause traced through: `authorizeApprovalButtonActor` → `isImplicitApprovalButtonActorAuthorized` → `resolveQQBotSlashCommandAuthorized` / `resolveSlashCommandAuth`
- The wildcard filter at `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/access/sender-match.ts` strips `"*"` entries, causing `explicitEntries.length === 0` → `return false` in `resolveSlashCommandAuth`
- Existing group-conversation tests continue to pass (gate remains for groups)
- New test cases cover the C2C direct conversation path with both no-allowlist and wildcard configurations

target.title: fix(memory): reject hex/exponent dreaming integer config strings
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where dreaming phase integer config fields silently accepted JavaScript-specific string forms (`0x10`, `1e3`, `2.5`) via `Number()` coercion. A user who wrote `"0x10"` for `phases.deep.limit` got a promotion limit of 16 instead of the shipped default 10.

The fix targets the `pluginValidation: "skip"` path used by `openclaw configure`, `openclaw doctor` migration, and config mutation flows. In these paths, AJV JSON Schema validation is intentionally skipped, so malformed integer strings bypass the manifest's `"type": "integer"` guard and reach the resolver directly. The normal config-loading path (AJV `"full"`) already rejects these strings — this fix closes the gap for skip-validation callers.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the shared `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` / `parseStrictPositiveInteger` helpers from `@openclaw/normalization-core/number-coercion`, which enforce `/^[+-]?\d+$/` — rejecting hex prefixes, exponent notation, and fractional dots at the contract level. Ordinary decimal strings (`"5"`) and numeric literals (`5`) keep working; malformed strings fall back to shipped defaults or omit optional fields.

Key design decisions:
- Delete the local `Number()`-based `normalizeNonNegativeInt` / `normalizeOptionalPositiveInt` entirely — no compat shims, no dual path
- `normalizeScore` (float scores 0–1) intentionally retains `Number()` — scores are not integers, and `Number("0.9")` is the correct parse
- The fix is a 2-line change per function (replace implementation body with shared helper call); the bulk of the diff is deleting the old 12-line bodies

Collision check: searched open PRs for `path:src/memory-host-sdk/dreaming.ts` — **0** competing PRs.

## User Impact

Malformed hex/exponent/fraction dreaming integer strings no longer silently change lookback windows, promotion limits, or token/timeout budgets. Valid decimal config is unchanged.

| Config field | Input | Before (`Number()`) | After (strict) | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `deep.limit` | `"0x10"` | 16 | **10** (fallback) | 10 |
| `deep.minRecallCount` | `"1e3"` | 1000 | **3** (fallback) | 3 |
| `deep.recencyHalfLifeDays` | `"1.5"` | 1 (floored) | **14** (fallback) | 14 |
| `deep.maxAgeDays` | `"0x20"` | 32 | **30** (fallback) | 30 |
| `deep.maxPromotedSnippetTokens` | `"1e2"` | 100 | **160** (fallback) | 160 |
| `deep.execution.maxOutputTokens` | `"0x40"` | 64 | **undefined** (omitted) | - |
| `deep.execution.timeoutMs` | `"1e4"` | 10000 | **undefined** (omitted) | - |
| `light.lookbackDays` | `"0x0a"` | 10 | **2** (fallback) | 2 |

## Verification

- Exact head: `b008cb8a2b92f1dfbd6abc4c62f30b65c11e36ff`
- `oxfmt --check src/memory-host-sdk/dreaming.ts src/memory-host-sdk/dreaming.test.ts` — passed.
- `oxlint src/memory-host-sdk/dreaming.ts src/memory-host-sdk/dreaming.test.ts` — passed; exit 0.
- `git diff --check` — passed; exit 0.
- Focused tests:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/memory-host-sdk/dreaming.test.ts -- --run
```

```

      Tests  16 passed (16)
```

- Mutation check: `git checkout origin/main -- src/memory-host-sdk/dreaming.ts` → 11 proof assertions fail (hex/exponent silently coerced) → restore fix → 31/31 pass.

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior addressed

Two layers:
1. **Normal config-loading path (`pluginValidation: "full"`):** AJV JSON Schema validation with `"type": "integer"` already rejects string values — config load fails with `"must be integer"` errors. The fix here is defense-in-depth.
2. **Skip-validation path (`pluginValidation: "skip"`):** Used by `openclaw configure`, doctor migration, and config mutation flows. AJV is intentionally bypassed, so malformed strings like `"0x10"` survive validation and reach `resolveMemoryDreamingConfig` as raw strings. The old `Number()` path silently coerced these into wrong values; the fix rejects them and falls back to defaults.

The proof exercises both the `"full"` and `"skip"` validation paths via the real `validateConfigObjectWithPlugins` function, then feeds the skip-validated plugin config through the real `resolveMemoryDreamingConfig` resolver.

### Evidence:

- **Old code silently coerces 10/10 fields:** `Number("0x10")` → 16, `Number("1e3")` → 1000, `Number("2.5")` → 2.5, etc.
- **Supported-path proof (case 2):** `pluginValidation: "full"` rejects malformed strings with `"must be integer"` (8 issues); `pluginValidation: "skip"` lets `"0x10"` pass through as a raw string — this is the path used by doctor/mutate/configure flows

- Live memory-core dreaming cron / narrative runs (this is config normalization only; cron behavior depends on resolved config shape which is unchanged for valid inputs)

- For the normal config-loading path, AJV already rejects these strings before they reach the resolver; the fix closes the gap for `pluginValidation: "skip"` callers (doctor, configure, mutate)
- Fallbacks preserve shipped defaults; no new config keys

target.title: fix(feishu): retry once on token-invalid errors 99991663/99991664 with cache invalidation (fixes #97287)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #97287.

When the cached `tenant_access_token` becomes invalid (e.g. clock drift, server-side revocation, or Feishu token expiry), the plugin cannot send messages. Error code `99991663 Invalid access token` is returned, but the plugin does not automatically refresh the token and retry. Users must manually restart the gateway to recover.

## Changes Made

- `extensions/feishu/src/comment-shared.ts`: Added `addFeishuTokenCacheClearer` / `clearFeishuTokenCaches`. `getFeishuTokenInvalidCode` detects 99991663/99991664. `requestFeishuApi` retries once on token-invalid (`retriedTokenInvalid` flag, independent of rate-limit budget). Fulfilled token-invalid bodies handled.
- `extensions/feishu/src/client.ts`: `createFeishuClient` creates a plugin-owned `Lark.Cache` via `buildSdkTokenCache()`. `clearClientCache` expires `CTenantAccessToken` in the private cache by appId namespace.
- `extensions/feishu/src/send.ts`: getter pattern — `opts.getClient()` inside request closure, ensures fresh client after cache clear.
- `extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.ts`: `clearFeishuTokenCache` registered. CardKit create retry on 99991663/99991664. Guarded-fetch release on non-JSON response.
- `extensions/feishu/src/client.test.ts`: NEW — client cache isolation tests.
- `extensions/feishu/src/send.retry.test.ts`: NEW — token-invalid + rate-limit retry sequence tests.
- `extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts`: NEW/UPDATED — card streaming tests including retry and guarded-fetch release.
- `extensions/feishu/src/token-retry-proof.test.ts`: NEW — end-to-end recovery proof tests (99991663/99991664 detection, cache clearing, getter pattern).

## Evidence

### 1. Production requestFeishuApi auto-retry on real 99991663 (7/7 passed)

Loads the ACTUAL `comment-shared.ts` module via `tsx` and exercises `requestFeishuApi` with a real 99991663 error. The production code automatically detects the token-invalid code, clears caches, and retries — all through the same code path that ships in the plugin.

```
 PRODUCTION requestFeishuApi AUTO-RETRY PROOF — PR #97295
 Host: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C
 Time: 2026-07-08T06:01:43Z
 Commit: 83830f71ec

─── 1. Real Feishu API: get token ───
  ✅ GET TOKEN: code=0
  ✅ BOT INFO:  code=0

─── 2. requestFeishuApi auto-retry on 99991663 ───
  ✅ Real API returns 99991663 with tampered token
  ✅ requestFeishuApi called 2x (1st=99991663, 2nd=success)
  ✅ Cache clear callback invoked (via addFeishuTokenCacheClearer)
  ✅ Recovered: result.code=0

─── 3. Cache isolation proof ───
  ✅ Fresh client after cache clear (different instance)

  RESULTS: 7/7 passed

  Production module exercised:
    extensions/feishu/src/comment-shared.ts
      → requestFeishuApi() — auto-retry on 99991663
      → getFeishuTokenInvalidCode() — detects 99991663/99991664
      → addFeishuTokenCacheClearer() — registers cache clearers
    extensions/feishu/src/client.ts
      → createFeishuClient() — builds SDK client
      → clearClientCache() — evicts CTenantAccessToken by namespace
```

### 2. Retry path steps (production code flow)

```
send() → 99991663 thrown
  → getFeishuTokenInvalidCode() detects 99991663
  → clearFeishuTokenCaches() → addFeishuTokenCacheClearer callbacks
  → clearClientCache() evicts CTenantAccessToken
  → retriedTokenInvalid = true (prevents infinite retry loop)
  → requestFeishuApi() RETRIES → SDK/fetch gets fresh token
  → send succeeds → code=0
```

### 3. Unit tests (113/113 passed)

```
 Test Files  5 passed (5)
 Tests       113 passed (113)
```

**Cache storage model**: All token caches are in-memory (Map + Lark.Cache), not persisted. No migration needed.

target.title: fix: keep image attachments when steering active runs
target.body:
Closes #107434

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who sent an image while an agent run was already active would have the steering text accepted but the image attachment dropped, so the running agent could not inspect the media.

## Why This Change Was Made

Active-run steering now carries the current turn's ordered image inputs through the shared queue contract and serializes the same sanitized text-and-image input shape for both new Codex turns and `turn/steer`; OpenClaw's embedded runtime receives the same images through its existing session steering API. The main regression risk is changing text-only pending-input handling, so media-bearing turns bypass that text-only answer path while focused tests retain the existing behavior for turns without images.

## User Impact

Users can attach images while a run is active and expect those images to reach the same running turn in order. If a runtime rejects steering, the existing follow-up fallback remains unchanged.

## Evidence

- Live after-fix proof on a local Gateway with the native Codex app-server runtime and `openai/gpt-5.4`:
  1. Started a turn that invoked a 35-second tool call.
  2. While that run was active, sent a second `chat.send` turn with a generated PNG containing the random code `A5C27F` and asked the model to return only the code in the image.
  3. The original active run completed with exactly `A5C27F`; session history showed the image-bearing user turn before that assistant response.
- The issue's source reproduction is covered at each boundary: reply queue admission, embedded-session steering, Codex steering serialization, and the full Codex run-attempt path.
- Focused tests: 278 passed across:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.media-paths.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.queue-message.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-steering.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.steering.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.test.ts`
- A clean Gateway launch rebuilt TypeScript and bundled plugin assets successfully; targeted `oxfmt` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Pre-commit autoreview reported no accepted or actionable findings.

AI-assisted: implementation and test review were assisted; the live behavior proof was run manually.

  • For performance and accuracy reasons, improved incremental analysis will now only be enabled on a pull request when diff-informed analysis is also enabled for that run.   • Added an experimental change which, when running a Code Scanning analysis for a PR with improved incremental analysis enabled, prefers CodeQL CLI versions that have a cached overlay-base database for the configured languages. This speeds up analysis for a repository when there is not yet a cached overlay-base database for the latest CLI version. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in May. #3880

4.35.4 - 07 May 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.4. #3881

4.35.3 - 01 May 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: Add a deprecation warning for customers using CodeQL version 2.19.3 and earlier. These versions of CodeQL were discontinued on 9 April 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.15, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. #3837
  • Configurations for private registries that use Cloudsmith or GCP OIDC are now accepted. #3850
  • Best-effort connection tests for private registries now use GET requests instead of HEAD for better compatibility with various registry implementations. For NuGet feeds, the test is now always performed against the service index. #3853
  • Fixed a bug where two diagnostics produced within the same millisecond could overwrite each other on disk, causing one of them to be lost. #3852

target.title: fix(secrets): use configured default agent ID in auth/model path discovery (#90573)
target.body:
## Summary

- Replace hard-coded `"main"` with `resolveDefaultAgentId(config)` in the two storage-scan helpers that seed path discovery (`listAuthProfileStoreAgentDirs`, `listAgentModelsJsonPaths`).
- Drop the `agentId === "main"` early-exit branches. Agents that declare a custom `agentDir` resolve through `resolveAgentDir(config, agentId)` (which honors the override); agents without one are scoped to the **passed** `stateDir` rather than the ambient process-env state dir, so scans stay confined to the requested root.
- Add 8 unit tests covering default-agent path inclusion and deduplication.

## Motivation

Closes #90573.

`listAuthProfileStoreAgentDirs()` and `listAgentModelsJsonPaths()` hard-coded `"main"` in two places each: the initial `paths.add()` seed and an `agentId === "main"` early-exit. In multi-agent deployments where the default agent is **not** `"main"` (e.g. `default: true` on a `"nova"` agent), this seeded a dead `agents/main/` path and ignored custom agent dirs.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** With a config whose default agent is `nova` (not `main`), `listAuthProfileStoreAgentDirs` / `listAgentModelsJsonPaths` previously seeded `agents/main/agent` and routed configured agents through the ambient-env state dir, so the requested `stateDir` was not honored for non-default agents. After the fix the default-agent seed uses the configured default agent id and every configured agent without a custom `agentDir` is scoped to the passed `stateDir`; custom `agentDir` overrides still win.

**Real environment tested:** Ran the shipped `src/secrets/auth-store-paths.ts` and `src/secrets/storage-scan.ts` modules directly on this checkout (macOS arm64, Darwin 25.4.0, Node v25.5.0) via the repo's `tsx`, with `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/oc-proof-state` and an isolated `HOME`. No mocks of the functions under test.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/oc-proof-state HOME=/tmp/oc-proof-home \
  npx tsx ./proof90603.mts
```

where `proof90603.mts` calls the two shipped exports with
`agents.list = [{id:"nova",default:true},{id:"main"},{id:"worker"}]`, then again with `nova` carrying `agentDir:"/opt/custom/nova"`.

**Evidence after fix (live stdout):**

```
== listAuthProfileStoreAgentDirs (nova default) ==
  /tmp/oc-proof-state/agents/nova/agent
  /tmp/oc-proof-state/agents/main/agent
  /tmp/oc-proof-state/agents/worker/agent
== listAgentModelsJsonPaths (nova default) ==
  /tmp/oc-proof-state/agents/nova/agent/models.json
  /tmp/oc-proof-state/agents/main/agent/models.json
  /tmp/oc-proof-state/agents/worker/agent/models.json
== custom agentDir honored ==
  /tmp/oc-proof-state/agents/nova/agent
  /opt/custom/nova
```

**Observed result after fix:** The `nova` default-agent path is seeded (no dead `main` seed when `main` is absent), all configured agents resolve under the **passed** `/tmp/oc-proof-state` root, and a custom `agentDir` (`/opt/custom/nova`) is honored verbatim instead of being rewritten under the state dir. This matches the regression suite (`src/secrets/auth-store-paths.default-agent.test.ts`, 8/8 passing).

**What was not tested:** Did not exercise the `resolveActiveAgentDir()` env-override fallback in `storage-scan.ts` (separate concern) or on-disk directory enumeration with real populated agent dirs; the live run uses a non-existent state dir so only the deterministic seed + configured-agent paths are asserted.

Closes the two deprecation windows opened by the channel-config refactor program, deleting the compat surface that exists only to warn external plugin authors: the streaming flat-key/scalar fallback (`streaming-flat-key-deprecation.ts` and friends) and the never-consumed `resolveGroupIntroHint` adapter surface.

Merging earlier would ship warning and removal in the same release, giving external plugins zero notice.

## Why This Change Was Made

The removal-plan comments in `streaming.ts` and `types.adapters.ts` name exactly this scope. Net **−442 LOC**: the four public streaming resolvers survive, rewritten nested-only and moved home to `streaming.ts` (single-use coercers inlined; file lands exactly at its ratcheted base of 1,210 lines); the warn-once module, leaf compat-entry type, scalar reads (shared, matrix monitor window, ACP), fallback-only tests, and the intro-hint adapter field + whatsapp export are deleted. target.title: fix(clawhub): reject calendar-invalid feed timestamps
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a malformed ClawHub promotions feed with an impossible calendar date (e.g. `2026-02-30T00:00:00.000Z`) would be accepted because `Date.parse` silently normalizes it. The feed parser would enter the normalized timestamp into cache state with an unintended expiry window.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuses `parseAbsoluteTimeMs` from `src/cron/parse.ts` — the same calendar validator adopted by the recent commitments fix (#106236) — to reject ISO timestamps whose calendar components are not real dates before they enter cache state. Both `generatedAt` and `expiresAt` are validated; numeric epoch strings remain rejected by the ISO-only feed contract, while canonical leap-day and normal ISO dates continue to parse without change.

## User Impact

Operators see no change under normal conditions (the live ClawHub feed emits canonical ISO timestamps). If a remote feed snapshot is ever malformed with an impossible date, it is now rejected instead of silently acquiring the wrong cache-expiry window, and the last accepted snapshot remains available.

## Evidence

**Before** (`upstream/main` at the PR base): `parseClawHubPromotionsFeed` accepted `generatedAt: "2026-02-30T00:00:00.000Z"` and returned the feed unchanged because `Date.parse` normalized the impossible date.

**Premise**: `parseAbsoluteTimeMs` validates the ISO calendar with a UTC component round trip. The feed parser keeps its ISO-only wire contract by excluding the helper's separate numeric-epoch input form.

**After — exact-head non-test runtime proof** (`40a0390b559bfde3eb8ceea226a1d85c59fb134c`):

I ran a standalone `node --import tsx --input-type=module -` script with an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`. The script started a real localhost HTTP server, pointed `OPENCLAW_CLAWHUB_URL` at it, and called the production `maybeRefreshPromotionsFeed` without an injected `fetchImpl`. The server first returned valid sequence 4 / ETag `"v4"`, then calendar-invalid sequence 5 / ETag `"v5"`. It was closed before the final cache read, so the final result came from the real SQLite state DB rather than HTTP. This did not load Vitest or set `NODE_ENV=test`.

```text
$ git rev-parse HEAD
40a0390b559bfde3eb8ceea226a1d85c59fb134c

$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$(mktemp -d /tmp/openclaw-pr106942-proof-XXXXXX)" node --import tsx --input-type=module -
{
  "runtime": { "vitest": null, "nodeEnv": null },
  "transport": {
    "realHttpRequests": 2,
    "requests": [
      { "url": "/api/v1/feeds/promotions", "ifNoneMatch": null },
      { "url": "/api/v1/feeds/promotions", "ifNoneMatch": "\"v4\"" }
    ]
  },
  "seeded": {
    "sequence": 4,
    "etag": "\"v4\"",
    "slugs": ["runtime-proof"]
  },
  "afterInvalid": {
    "sequence": 4,
    "etag": "\"v4\"",
    "slugs": ["runtime-proof"]
  },
  "sqliteReadAfterServerClosed": {
    "sequence": 4,
    "etag": "\"v4\"",
    "slugs": ["runtime-proof"]
  }
}
```

This demonstrates that the invalid response reached the production HTTP → parser → SQLite cache path, was rejected, and did not replace the last accepted snapshot. A subsequent read after the HTTP server was closed still returned sequence 4 / ETag `"v4"` from SQLite.

target.title: fix(slack): suppress progress chrome sends
target.body:
## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of `chat.postMessage`
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies
- type automatic tool-progress payloads at the producer boundary with a closed generic plugin-SDK progress intent so Slack does not infer from arbitrary text

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: \`pnpm test\`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Evidence
Current head: `1e3f34f78d97ec5790a39b722f55b53e640488c5`.

- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false vitest run --project extension-codex extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` passed (149 tests)
- focused Slack replies + identity-fallback tests passed (85 tests)
- `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` passed (10 tests)
- `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false tsgo:extensions` passed
- formatter check on touched files passed
- `git diff --check` passed

## Public SDK Contract
This PR uses a closed generic progress-intent contract on the reply-payload surface:

- shared field: `channelData.openclawProgressKind`
- generic tool progress kind: `TOOL_PROGRESS_KIND = "tool-progress"`
- generic predicate: `isToolProgressPayload`
- existing fast-mode kind remains: `FAST_MODE_AUTO_PROGRESS_KIND = "fast-mode-auto"`

Codex no longer exports Codex-named public progress symbols. Codex marks only transient automatic tool summaries with the generic `tool-progress` kind; completed/failed/verbose terminal output is left unmarked and remains deliverable. Callable public SDK budget was raised with the additive predicate.

target.title: fix(cli): bound --message-file reads for agent command
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readAgentMessageFile` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts` used `fs.readFile(messageFile)` with no size limit. A user (or a symlink attack) pointing `--message-file` at a multi-gigabyte file could exhaust CLI memory before the message is validated or dispatched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Agent messages are prompt text; a 4 MiB cap is generous headroom for long system prompts while preventing an unbounded local-file read from OOMing the gateway/embedded dispatch path. The existing error formatting is preserved so callers still see familiar ENOENT/EISDIR messages.

## User Impact

- `openclaw agent --message-file <path>` now rejects files larger than 4 MiB with a clear size-limit error.
- Normal message files continue to work unchanged, including UTF-8 BOM stripping.
- The gateway is never reached with an oversized message file.

## Evidence

- Replaced `readFile` with `readRegularFile({ filePath: messageFile, maxBytes: AGENT_MESSAGE_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts`.
- Added a regression test in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` asserting that a 5 MiB message file is rejected before `callGateway` is invoked.
- Lint and core typecheck pass locally. Full test suite will run on the PR CI.

## Real behavior proof

I created a 5 MiB message file and a directory path and ran `agentCliCommand` with `--message-file`. The CLI rejects both before any gateway dispatch:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |commands| src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts (74 tests) 4412ms
     ✓ rejects message files that exceed the size cap
     ✓ reports a directory message file with the legacy EISDIR message
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  70 passed (70)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 17.16s
```

- The oversized file is rejected with `File exceeds 4194304 bytes` and `callGateway` is never invoked.
- A directory path still reports `Message file is a directory:` preserving the existing CLI UX.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

Ran a standalone Node script outside Vitest that imports the real `readRegularFile` helper re-exported by `src/infra/regular-file.ts` (the same helper now used by `readAgentMessageFile`) and exercises normal, oversized, and directory inputs:

```text
PR #101442 standalone real-behavior proof
Temp root: /tmp/proof-101442-24382397-303b-4df6-9e58-5fb8b44c202a

  Normal file read ... OK: decoded="Hello from PR #101442.\n"
  Oversized file rejects ... OK: File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442/huge.md
  Directory rejects as non-regular ... OK: path must be a regular file
  Directory preserves legacy EISDIR UX ... OK: Message file is a directory: /tmp/proof-101442/not-a-file

All real-behavior checks passed.
```

Command used:

```text
node --import ./node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs /tmp/proof-101442.mjs
```

The script is intentionally not committed to the repo and lives at `/tmp/proof-101442.mjs`.



## Real behavior proof (standalone CLI)

I ran the real `openclaw agent --message-file` CLI path (via `pnpm openclaw`) against four temp inputs:

**1. Normal message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/normal.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 40130106-91a0-47f3-ba23-fa79a807f5c0 ended with stopReason=aborted
```
The CLI read the file and started the agent turn (aborted because no model provider was configured).

**2. Oversized message file (5 MiB, cap is 4 MiB)**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
Error: Unable to read message file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md: File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md | File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md
[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.
```
The CLI rejected the file before any gateway dispatch or model call.

**3. Single-symlink message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/symlink.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 9bf5fd4e-8aae-4561-bb6a-4a1ad01be49e ended with stopReason=stop
```
The symlink was followed and the agent turn started.

**4. Chained-symlink message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/link-b.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 94342b49-9153-4f1a-bc8f-fa3a0ccbbb44 ended with stopReason=stop
```
The full symlink chain was resolved and the agent turn started.

The implementation now uses `fs.realpath` before the bounded read, so legacy symlinked `--message-file` paths continue to work while oversized files are rejected before dispatch.

target.title: fix(shared): bound ignore-file reads during workspace scans
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`addIgnoreRules` in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts` reads `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.fdignore` files with `readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size limit. A malicious or runaway ignore file in a scanned workspace can be loaded entirely into memory, causing the CLI or agent workspace scan to OOM before any rules are applied.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ignore files are line-oriented pattern lists; even large monorepos rarely exceed a few hundred KiB. Adding a 4 MiB byte cap lets legitimate ignore files pass through while preventing an unbounded read from exhausting process memory. The existing `catch` block means oversized files are skipped silently, matching the current graceful behavior for unreadable files.

## User Impact

- Workspace scans (`openclaw agent`, skill loading, etc.) no longer buffer arbitrarily large ignore files.
- Oversized `.gitignore` / `.ignore` / `.fdignore` files are skipped instead of crashing the process.
- Normal-sized ignore files work exactly as before.

## Evidence

- Replaced `readFileSync` with `readRegularFileSync({ filePath, maxBytes: IGNORE_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts`.
- Added `src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts` with regression tests covering normal ignore files, large-but-under-cap files, and files that exceed the cap.
- Local test run:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts --run
  # 3 tests passed
  ```

## Real behavior proof

I created `.gitignore` files at, above, and below the new 4 MiB cap, plus a symlinked `.gitignore` pointing to a regular file, and ran workspace scan ignore-rule loading:


- A 13 MiB ignore file is silently skipped instead of buffering the whole file.
- A symlinked `.gitignore` is resolved and its regular target is still honored, preserving the previous workspace-scan behavior.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

I ran a standalone Node script that imports `addIgnoreRules` from `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts` and exercises normal, large-but-under-cap, oversized, single-symlink, and chained-symlink `.gitignore` files in temp workspaces:

## What Problem This Solves

`shouldSuggestMemorySystem` and `migrateLegacyRootMemoryFile` in `src/commands/doctor-workspace.ts` read `AGENTS.md`, `MEMORY.md`, and archived `memory.md` with unbounded `fs.promises.readFile(..., "utf-8")`. ## User Impact

- `openclaw doctor` workspace memory checks no longer buffer arbitrarily large files.
- Oversized `AGENTS.md` / memory files are handled gracefully instead of crashing.
- Normal workspace doctor flows work exactly as before.

## Evidence

- Replaced unbounded `fs.promises.readFile` calls with `readRegularFile` capped reads in `src/commands/doctor-workspace.ts`.
- Added regression tests in `src/commands/doctor-workspace.test.ts` covering an oversized `AGENTS.md` and an oversized legacy memory file.
- Local test run:
  ```

  # 5 tests passed
  ```

I created a standalone Node script at `/tmp/proof-101448.mjs` that imports the real helpers from `src/commands/doctor-workspace.ts` and exercises both the normal and oversized paths in isolated temp workspaces:

```text

Normal AGENTS.md -> shouldSuggestMemorySystem = false
```
